reason: Every colour must come from a --vscode-* variable with a visible fallback, no new runtime dependency and no asset file, and every subscription disposed - the rules this UI change is most likely to break.
The change lives entirely in src/editor/ plus one setting; src/core must stay untouched, and this records why that boundary exists.

The test host has no webview DOM, so most of this work is asserted on the rendered markup - and the rule that an assertion must fail when the feature is deleted is what keeps those markup assertions from being tautological.
The provider, the webview message protocol and the current reveal mechanism are all being changed here; this is the contract they were built to.
The value widget registers its click and key handlers first and claims events with stopImmediatePropagation; the new click model must keep that contract intact.
Parent sections 6 (display rules - what must not change), 9 (editor), 10 (navigation) and 11 (contributions, where the new setting is declared).
Collapse state, scroll position and focus live on both sides of the webview/host boundary, and the re-scan round-trip is where they get lost.
The reader-facing description of the interaction model and settings; it must end up true.
